key_insight: Evaluator bias in LLM multi-agent systems can spread through the agent network, and the paper formalizes this contagion with measurable coefficients and regimes.
engineering_relevance: For multi-agent AI systems, using larger or more balanced evaluator committees can substantially reduce bias propagation, improving reliability of coordinated LLM workflows.
method: Defines Contagion Networks to quantify cross-agent bias spread.
Runs a controlled 3-agent experiment with DeepSeek-chat under structured, balanced, and evidence-based evaluator profiles.
Measures a Cross-Agent Contagion Matrix Gamma_3 and relates propagation behavior to the spectral radius rho(Gamma_N).
evidence_signal: In the abstract’s 3-agent experiment, contagion coefficients remained positive at gamma = 0.157–0.352, and increasing committee size from k=1 to k=3 reduced effective contagion by 72.4%.
watch_item: Results are from a controlled setup on a single underlying model and may not generalize to larger, more heterogeneous, or dynamically changing multi-agent deployments.
paper_title: Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
